titulo: HyperFrames from scratch: HTML with data-* becomes MP4
lead: HyperFrames is an open engine from HeyGen that renders HTML into video. Three attributes set the size and duration, a paused GSAP timeline sets the motion, and the check verifies everything before the render. In this lesson you create the project, write the first composition, and walk away with a verified MP4.
objetivo: create a HyperFrames project, write the composition with data-*, and render an MP4 that passes the checker.

aprende.t: What init creates and why the version is pinned in package.json
The root with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration
The paused GSAP timeline registered in window.__timelines
check, render, and the kit's checker

hero_alt: An open laptop on a dark desk showing a dark video frame, with a reference monitor beside it.

nos.detalhe: npx hyperframes@0.8.176 init creates index.html, package.json (with the version pinned in the scripts), hyperframes.json, and an AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md with the rules for the agent.
The root carries data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration (in seconds). An element with data-start becomes a clip that appears only during its interval.
A single gsap.timeline({ paused: true }) registered in window.__timelines["main"], with the same key as the data-composition-id. The engine moves that timeline to each instant.
Runs the lint and opens the composition in a browser: runtime errors, text outside the frame, motion, and contrast. Only render once you see Check passed.
--quality draft for testing, looks (default) and delivery for final output. --workers limits how many Chrome instances run at the same time.

secoes.legenda: When the root has data-duration, it rules: a shorter timeline holds the last frame.

secoes.sub: init without prompts (--non-interactive) and telemetry turned off before anything else.

blocos.rot: Terminal · create the project and see what came out
blocos.conteudo:
export HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 NO_COLOR=1
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-motion/a2; rm -rf "$E"; mkdir -p "$E"; cd "$E"
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 init minha-abertura --non-interactive > init.log 2>&1; echo "saída: $?"
ls minha-abertura
grep '"render"' minha-abertura/package.json
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 telemetry status | head -2

The render script in package.json already calls the exact version. Telemetry shows as disabled because the block exported HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1.

By default the CLI sends anonymous usage data. telemetry status in 0.8.176 shows how to turn it off: hyperframes telemetry disable (saved permanently) or the variables HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1 (current session only). The course blocks use the variable.

blocos.rot: Terminal · check, render, and run the checker
blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/formacao-cinema-ia-motion-v72/kit
export HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 NO_COLOR=1
cd ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-motion/a2/minha-abertura
cp "$K/exemplos/a2-ola/index.html" index.html
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 check 2>&1 | grep -E "◇|✗|⚠"
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 render --quality draft --workers 2 --quiet --output renders/abertura.mp4 > render.log 2>&1
echo "render: $?"
python3 "$K/conferir.py" renders/abertura.mp4 5 1920x1080; echo "saída: $?"

The first five ◇ lines are the parts of the check (lint, execution, layout, motion, contrast); the sixth, disabled, is frame capture, which comes turned off (--snapshots turns it on). The checker reads the MP4 with ffprobe and compares it with what you asked for: 5 s, 1920×1080.

abas.rot: Common mistake: a clip with children
abas.html: Putting data-start on a section that has a title and text inside made the 0.8.176 lint warn nested_structure_needs_subcomposition. In the example, the section is just a container (no data-start) and the timeline animates the children; a scene with several elements of its own becomes a subcomposition.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: What sets the MP4's duration in HyperFrames?
opcoes: The length of the GSAP timeline.
The duration of the longest clip.
perguntas.explica: The root rules: a shorter timeline holds the last frame, and a clip with a data-start that runs past the end is cut off (the lint warns with clip_ends_past_root_duration). Without data-duration, the engine infers the duration from the timeline.

perguntas.p: The check passed, but the render came out wrong. Which of these does the check NOT guarantee?
opcoes: That no JavaScript errors are running on the page.
That no text spills outside the frame.
That the video tells the right story.
That the text contrast passes WCAG AA.
perguntas.explica: The check covers the technical side: execution, layout, motion, contrast. Whether the piece says the right thing is up to you, by looking at the frames (lesson 3).

perguntas.p: Why does the course pin hyperframes@0.8.176 in every command?
opcoes: So the block gives the same output months from now.
Because newer versions stopped rendering MP4.
Because npx won't let you run another version.
So you don't have to download the browser again.
perguntas.explica: The package changes every week (the older courses used 0.8.66). A pinned version in the block and in the init's package.json is what keeps the captured output valid.

perguntas.p: How do you turn off telemetry only for the terminal session?
opcoes: By deleting the ~/.hyperframes folder on your machine.
By running every command with the --quiet option.
By uninstalling the Chrome that the render downloaded.
perguntas.explica: Both variables turn it off for as long as the session lasts; hyperframes telemetry disable saves the choice. --quiet only cuts the text on screen.
